description: In the push-rejection retry branch of `publishLedgerCycle()` (ledger-publish.mjs:672-692), `pushed = true` is set UNCONDITIONALLY after the retry's try block completes, regardless of whether an actual `git push` call was made. The push is only re-issued `if (result.pendingLineCount > 0)` (line 683-685); if the post-reset re-reconciliation finds `pendingLineCount === 0` (e.g. an ambiguous network failure where the FIRST push attempt actually landed on the remote before the client saw a non-zero exit/timeout, or a genuine outside divergence that happened to already contain everything this cycle wanted to publish), the code falls through to `pushed = true;` on line 686 having never called `git push` in this branch. `lastPushTs`/`publishFailureStreak` are then updated purely off this over-broad `pushed` flag (lines 694-697: `if (pushed) { lastPushTs = nowMs; publishFailureStreak = 0; }`), not off any direct confirmation that a push actually executed this cycle. While the specific reachable instances I traced end up benign in isolation (the `confirmedThisCycle = pushed && result.committed` gate on lines 702-708 happens to prevent the *cursor* from being advanced incorrectly in the sub-case where `result.committed` is also false), the RETURNED `result.pushed` value and the persisted `lastPushTs`/`publishFailureStreak` state can misreport a push as having happened when no `git push` command actually ran in that code path -- a caller or healthcheck relying on `pushed:true` to mean 'a push was attempted and observed to succeed this cycle' receives a false signal in this branch. The fix is a one-line correctness issue: `pushed` should only be set true inside the `if (result.pendingLineCount > 0)` block (immediately after the `git push` call succeeds), not unconditionally after the surrounding try block.

corroborating.note: lastPushTs/publishFailureStreak reset off the bare `pushed` flag, and the wakePushedLineCount/earnPushedLineCount cursor advance is gated by `confirmedThisCycle = pushed && result.committed` -- the cursor happens to be protected by the second half of this AND, but `pushed`/`lastPushTs`/`publishFailureStreak` are not.

the only divergence/retry test (FIND-002 divergence) always has pendingLineCount>0 after reset, so this specific fallthrough (retry succeeds structurally but issues zero actual push calls) is never exercised by any test in the suite.
